extracted.intended_audience: new and existing users of Mathematics Stack Exchange (people who ask and answer math questions on the site)
extracted.subtask_description: The Help Center landing page summarises site norms and pointers for asking and answering mathematical questions, community behaviour, formatting, reputation/voting, moderation actions, and related account/tools. It is an index to the detailed help articles users should read to participate correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: How the site works
rubrics_metrics.description: "Here's how it works: Anybody can ask a question. Anybody can answer. The best answers are voted up and rise to the top.", (Take the 2-minute tour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core Q&A model: community-driven question asking and answering; answers are ranked by votes. The page links to the short tour for a concise overview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be nice (expected behavior)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-line behavioural standard; points to further help about what kind of behaviour is expected of users (code of conduct / civility guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: On-topic scope
rubrics_metrics.description: "What topics can I ask about here?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates there are site-specific topicality rules (what is considered on-topic for Mathematics SE); detailed boundaries are in the linked help article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of questions to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: "What types of questions should I avoid asking?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site has question-types that are discouraged or off-topic; the linked help article lists examples and anti-patterns (e.g., overly broad, opinion-based, unclear).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question closure and 'on hold' status
rubrics_metrics.description: "What does it mean if a question is 'closed' or 'on hold'?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains closure reasons and the temporary 'on hold' status; guidance and remediation steps are in the linked article.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to ask a good question
rubrics_metrics.description: "How do I ask a good question?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signpost to criteria for a well-asked question (clarity, context, showing effort, reproducible statements, minimal necessary information) — full guidance is in the linked help page.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to do after someone answers
rubrics_metrics.description: "What should I do when someone answers my question?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes accepting answers, commenting, giving feedback, and follow-up; detailed etiquette and mechanics are in the linked article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics formatting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag that mathematical notation/formatting guidance is provided (e.g., MathJax/LaTeX usage); users should follow the linked formatting guide for readable math.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation and voting
rubrics_metrics.description: "Why is voting important? What is reputation? How do I earn (and lose) it?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes that voting is the primary mechanism for content evaluation and reputation is the rough measure of community trust; details on reputation changes and voting mechanics are in the linked help pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounties
rubrics_metrics.description: "What is a bounty? How can I start one?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the optional reputation-based reward mechanism to attract attention to questions and how to offer/start a bounty; procedural details live in the linked article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: "What does it mean when an answer is 'accepted'?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies the meaning and effects of the question author accepting an answer (marks solution, awards reputation), with specifics in the help center.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to write a good answer
rubrics_metrics.description: "How do I write a good answer?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signposts quality criteria for answers (correctness, clarity, explanation, showing work, citations when appropriate); full advice is in the linked help page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: "How to reference material written by others"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates there are norms for citing and attributing others' work; the linked help article explains acceptable quotation, attribution, and plagiarism rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer deletion and account answer restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Why are answers no longer being accepted from my account? Why and how are some answers deleted?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to moderation and automatic system restrictions (answer bans, deletion reasons) and the process/criteria for deletion; users should consult the linked moderation help for remediation and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badges and privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: "Badges — View a full list of badges you can earn" and "Privileges — View a full list of privileges you can earn"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the existence of gamification/privilege thresholds tied to reputation and actions; the badge and privilege pages list criteria and thresholds for earning them.
